question: If knowledge arises in an all-pervading self but only in one part, body, or mind, does that make the self divisible?
premises: Knowledge is said to arise in an all-pervading self.
To avoid overgeneralization, it may be restricted to one part, the body, or the mind.
Such restriction implies division or parts.
inference: Restricting knowledge within an all-pervading self entails an unwanted partite state of the self.
plain_english: If knowledge arises in an all-pervading self, but only in one part, or only in the body, or again only in the mind, then the self would have a state composed of parts.
